quest.title: The Unappreciated Carving
quest.description: For reasons unknown, two craftsmen are sighing over a unique carving in the open market of Port Ormos...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x80, Mora x20000, Exquisite Kamera x1, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Port Ormos is pretty great! There's so many new and interesting things, not to mention all the tasty food!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sumeru's largest commercial port sure lives up to its name! Look at all the merchants, and everyone seems excited just to be here.

choices.text: Not everyone, I'm sure.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: *sigh* How did things end up like this?

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: All thanks to your "artistic license," that's how. I should've made you wait until we got an update from Tanger.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: But when I finished the Prototype Aranara yesterday, you agreed that the kids would like it! That's why we tried bringing it out for a test run today.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: Well... I never thought they'd dislike it so much.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: *sigh* What should we do...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There we go. They sound distinctly less than excited.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, yeah, compared to everyone else, they seem really down in the dumps! Let's go find out what's going on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey there! Paimon's name's Paimon, and {NICKNAME}'s a traveler who was just passing by. Is there something bothering you?

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: Oh! I noticed you two a moment ago. Welcome to Acara Crafts, the best toy store in Port Ormos... at least for now.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: What's bothering us is this Prototype Aranara... To start with, could I get your opinion on it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Prototype Aranara"? Uh, you mean this wood-carving here? Looks like a mushroom monster to Paimon.

choices.text: Sounds like the name of a weapon.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: No, no, the Prototype Aranara is something that brings joy and laughter to children... at least, in theory.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: Not the first negative feedback we've had.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what exactly is a Prototype Aranara?

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: So for context, Aranara are magical creatures in Sumeru fairytales that live in the forest.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: For the store's 20th anniversary, we planned to release a series of hand-carved toys based on the Aranara stories that kids know and love.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: This is a prototype we made to get an idea of how they would react.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: But when we put it out there... the reaction was... not quite what we'd anticipated.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They thought it looked like a mushroom too, huh?

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: No, worse than that, actually... I can't quite describe it though, and I'm also not very good with kids. Maybe you could ask them for yourselves?

response.speaker: Qasit
response.text: This is not an Aranara! No way!

response.speaker: Qasit
response.text: I've read Uncle Tanger's "Aranara and the Ill Little Fungus," it says that Aranara are supposed to be chubby and squishy. The carving looks nothing like that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, toys do look better when they're round and chubby.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Uncle Tanger said in "Aranara's Vow" that you can deceive the eyes, but you can't deceive the heart.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: This carving makes me feel lost and confused inside... I don't think the creator put his heart into it at all. It's nothing like an Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Didn't put his heart into it, huh? Sounds like one of those things that's easier said than understood.

response.speaker: Ruhi
response.text: Qasit and Alia didn't like this carving, but I think it's okay.

response.speaker: Ruhi
response.text: It doesn't look too happy, so it's kind of pitiful in a cute way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! A positive review!

response.speaker: Ruhi
response.text: Yeah! So I would totally ask my dad to get it for me... if it wasn't meant to be an Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Well that took a sudden turn for the worse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We asked the children for their opinions.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: How did it go? Has it maybe... grown on them at all?

choices.text: Unfortunately, no.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: Oh, this is such a shame... Why isn't Tanger back from Gandharva Ville yet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! The kids kept mentioning an "Uncle Tanger," too. Who is he, exactly?

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: "Uncle Tanger" is a famous children's author here in Port Ormos.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: He wrote quite a few stories in the past, but none of them were popular among children. Just like our Prototype Aranara.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: But around a year or so ago, he suddenly had a eureka moment or something, and suddenly the children loved every one of his stories.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: That's right. My little Ghafari loves his stories too. The whole reason we decided to make these carvings was because we saw just how popular the Aranara are among children.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: We asked Tanger for guidance, but right after he agreed, he went off to Gandharva Ville with his son to look for inspiration. They haven't returned yet.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: We were running out of time, so we had no choice but to carve an Aranara based on our own imaginations.

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: As you can see, this was the result... *sigh*

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: *sigh* We have to do something...

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: Hey, since you're the famous Traveler, could you do us a favor and look for Tanger in Gandharva Ville?

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: He doesn't have to come in person if he's too busy. Just ask him to write down his suggestions and bring his notes back to us, if you could.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: Please, if only to put a smile on the children's faces... And of course, you'll be well compensated for doing us the favor!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #They seem pretty desperate. {NICKNAME}, let's help them out to see the kids' smiles and also for our reward.

choices.text: Okay, we'll do it to see the kids smile.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! Let's do it!

choices.text: Okay, we'll do it so that Paimon can get her rewards.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay! Rewards!

choices.text: I'm starting to understand how you feel.
But it doesn't look very happy.

response.speaker: Mamdouh
response.text: *sigh*... There we have it, the verdict is in. What a headache.

choices.text: No one quite as excited as Paimon.

talks.objective: Go to Gandharva Ville and find Tanger

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe he's a genius who spends a lot of time in solitary confinement.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Tanger's just a normal guy....

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Even so, he must be more creative than most people.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wait, hold on! Razi, do you mean you've met Tanger before?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm... He's my dad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your dad!? Tanger's your dad? As in, you're Tanger's son?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon sees! That guy at Acara Crafts told us that Tanger brought his son along with him. So he meant Razi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you here on your own, though? Did you and Tanger get separated?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I... We had an argument... I was upset, so I ran off here by myself...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, in that case... We should take you back to Gandharva Ville first. Then we'll look for your dad and tell him where you are.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: No, I'm good! Thanks for your advice, Collei. I'm not so upset anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Come with me. I'll take you to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, thanks Razi! Paimon thought we'd be spending the whole day looking for him!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh my gosh, I can't believe I'm actually gonna meet "the" Tanger!

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Oh, Razi! Thank goodness, I finally found you! What would I do without you, my son?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Were you in danger? Did the wild beasts scare you? Did the stars guide your way?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I'm okay... All thanks to their help.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Thank you! Thank you all! I dare say that even the most cold-hearted Spinocrocodile would be moved to tears by your kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, it's nothing. It's all part of my responsibility as a Trainee Forest Ranger. I'm the one who should thank you for creating so many wonderful stories for the children of Sumeru. I... I love them too!

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Really? I didn't know anyone read my stories apart from young children. That must mean you're still in touch with your inner child!

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Hmm, okay then... I have the inspiration for my next story. It shall be about an Aranara granny who's a child at heart!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It's... it's an honor to become the source of your inspiration!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Collei looks like she's about to pass out... Uhh, hey Collei, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm okay. Sorry, I just got a little too excited.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Are you two story lovers as well? Yes... Yes! The moment I saw you, the image of an Aragiant and an Arafinch traveling together popped into my mind!

choices.text: We've been tasked with seeking your help.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Oh? Who asked for my help? My sincerest apologies, but I have fans all over Sumeru... Trying to remember every last one is like trying to identify each grain of sand in the desert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... Seems like Tanger has a slightly exaggerated view of what it means to be a children's author...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, Paimon's not a finch! That's nothing to get excited about.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's put the jokes aside and get down to business.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Tanger about the situation at Acara Crafts.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Acara Crafts... Acara Crafts...

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Oh! Oh right, right! I remember now. That small boat once sailed into the sea of my memory, but before long, it floated away over the horizon, never to be seen again.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Perhaps for the best: After all, a wild tempest was a-raging in Tanger Harbor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, what? Paimon has no idea what he's saying...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Me neither.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do? Do you think we should get Tighnari to take a look at him?

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: Dad's saying he forgot about helping the people at Acara Crafts learn more about Aranara, because right now, he has something more important to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, THAT's what he meant... Well, there it is, all the proof you needed that this kid is definitely Tanger's son.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, no, this isn't the time for all that. Tanger, your help is pretty vital to the toymakers. You gotta do something!

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: But the garden that blooms before my eyes is of greater importance. For therein lies the beautiful Padisarah that all the children of Sumeru dream of.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: I, Tanger, have found evidence of Aranara activity right here in the Avidya Forest! Conclusively proving that Aranara not only exist in stories, but in real life too!

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: If I manage to document the first real-life Aranara sighting, the petty problems that perplex Acara Crafts will be untangled in no time.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Meanwhile, I may well be able to leverage this to assume leadership of the Akademiya. Then, all across Sumeru will know of the great Tanger living in humble Port Ormos!

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: ...*sigh*.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Um...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I haven't written any papers myself, but I think you need to have a bunch of them approved by the review board before entering the Akademiya. You also need a detailed and objective experiment record.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Anyway, Tanger, what did you mean by "evidence of Aranara activity"?

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: The hook's what's important in a story! The great storyteller Tanger never gives his audience the bait right away! Come with me!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Wait! Not that way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Collei, what's wrong?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Nothing, but that way leads us deeper into the Avidya Forest. I'm just concerned for Tanger's safety.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: And I think I'm starting to understand why Razi and Tanger were fighting...

choices.text: (Maybe there's something else going on.)
(Maybe that's the secret Razi was keeping...)
Yup, I'm the Aragiant and she's the Arafinch!

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Ah, excellent, improvisation! Yes, mount your trusty steed of imagination and canter through the lush meadows of lyrical expression... you have the potential to become a celebrated storyteller too, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Just as I expected, the promise of one of my stories has kept you hot on my heels.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But this is just an ordinary tree hollow. Paimon's not seeing any evidence of Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: "You can deceive the eyes, but you can't deceive the heart." Look with your heart and you, too, will understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Paimon's not sure what "look with your heart" means, but anyway, let's start by investigating the area around this tree hollow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey look, there's a note here. Could this be the evidence that Tanger was talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, the handwriting's so hard to read. "It's too hard! I can't remember the names of all these mushrooms"...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do Aranara need to learn about mushroom classification...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here's another note that says, "This tree hollow is my castle."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds more like something an Aranara from the stories would say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's another one here! Hmm... "If only I were a clever Aranara."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A clever Aranara... Is the emphasis on "clever," or "Aranara"?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: How does it feel to bear witness to a groundbreaking discovery? Exciting, isn't it?

choices.text: What's so groundbreaking about it?

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: The crude handwriting may look like a child's, but don't forget, we're in the middle of a rainforest.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: I doubt that a child would be able to reach this deep into the forest, and I doubt even more that they would think of this lowly tree hollow as some sort of impenetrable castle.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: I boldly hypothesize that this tree hollow is in fact the Aranara's Akademiya. The notes we saw were written by the Aranara themselves. There is no doubt in my mind about that.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: An Aranara that wasn't so bright left a note here wishing to become a "clever Aranara."

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: I shall craft a new story for them and call it "The Aranara in the Tree Hollow"!

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: How's that? Don't the very words just conjure up images of Aranara in your mind's eye?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, nope...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not at all...

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Well, many an adventurer knows how to take to the skies with their easily visible wind gliders, yet they do not possess the invisible wings of imagination, making it hard for them to keep up with my train of thought.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: How about you, Miss Forest Ranger? Do you soar into the atmosphere on the wings of imagination?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Huh!? Me? I don't know... Maybe I do, but maybe not. Anyway... it has nothing to do with me, so...

choices.text: Collei, is everything okay?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Yeah, I'm fine. It's just that... witnessing Tanger's creative process is a little... um...

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Overwhelming?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh yes, yes, overwhelming.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: For now, I've decided to stay here with Razi until we witness the legendary moment when the Aranara appear in this hollow.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Don't worry, I won't let the Acara Crafts toymakers down. When a real Aranara appears, their little troubles will be resolved in an instant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He seems pretty stubborn. Looks like we'll have to stay here and wait a little longer.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: No. I think we should return to our camp first.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Tanger, in "Aranara and the Ill Little Fungus," it says that Aranara are very sensitive creatures. I don't think they'll show up if we stay here.

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: Oh? Was that in the story? Ah... yes, I remember now. Miss Forest Ranger, you sure know your stuff!

response.speaker: Tanger
response.text: In that case, let's go back to camp and call it a day. We'll continue our search for evidence first thing in the morning.

choices.text: Are you sure you're not feeling unwell?
They looked like messages left by children.

talks.objective: Go to the encampment at night (00:00 – 4:00 the next day)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, {NICKNAME}, wake up.

choices.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not the Aranara, it's Collei... She's gone!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's been worried about Collei since last night. Even though she kept telling us she was okay, after we saw the "evidence of Aranara activity," she's been acting kinda strange.

choices.text: I noticed that too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's go find her.

choices.text: Maybe Tanger was too much for her.
Did the Aranara show up?

talks.objective: Approach the hollow and examine it

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Collei came back here alone. Is she waiting for the Aranara to show up?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #*sniff* And I thought this was a place nobody knew about... I never thought Tanger would find it, or that I would run into {NICKNAME} and Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: *sob* If I'd known, I would have just told the tree hollow instead of writing it down! There must be another way to practice my handwriting...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Now I've created a whole new problem for myself... What do I do now, dress up as an Aranara...?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, that won't work. I should be writing something that an Aranara would never say so that Tanger won't mistake me for one of them.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But what should I write? What should I write...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh! I've got it! There's no way Tanger could see this as the work of an Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the "evidence of Aranara activity" we saw during the day, was actually... evidence of Collei's activity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why didn't she just tell Tanger?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps that's her secret.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! Collei told Razi that he could tell any secret to a tree hollow. Must be because that's what she does, and now she even writes it down.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Collei must have her reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're right. We'll keep her secret for her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like she's almost done writing. Let's head back.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Aha! There's a new note, just as I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! It's the same handwriting, which means it must've been written by the same Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Let's see what it says...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, what could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: "I want to visit Mondstadt during the Ludi Harpastum again"...?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: No, that's impossible! This must be some kind of mistake! How could an Aranara go to Mondstadt for the Ludi Harpastum?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Even I would never write that into a fairy tale!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So in other words, the notes can't have been left by an Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah! If you ask me, they were probably left by a passing merchant from Mondstadt or something. Definitely not an Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: No! No, I refuse to believe it!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Despite his denial, Tanger falls into a deep silence when faced by the facts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please help Acara Crafts.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: I can't...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean you can't? It's not like it'll take you a huge amount of effort.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You've written so many stories beloved by the children. I'm sure you can help create carvings that are just as successful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I believe in you, Tanger.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: No! I can't do it!

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: I thought that if I could find an Aranara, I'd be able to help Acara Crafts.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: But it was someone from Mondstadt all along...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But you managed to write all those stories without ever having seen a real Aranara, right? What makes this so different?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: *sigh* Razi, you tell them.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Really? Can I?

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Yes, it's fine. Tell them, I know this is the moment you've been waiting for.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: #Collei, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Do you remember when I said that there was a secret I didn't wanna tell anyone?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yup, I do.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I didn't want to tell anyone the secret, but it made me feel very sad and also turned Dad into a completely different person.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: So... I think I should tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Dad isn't the one who came up with all those Aranara stories.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: What? Hold on, so if Uncle Tanger wasn't the author, then... who was it? Ah, wait, you don't mean...

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: It was me.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Dad's been telling stories in Port Ormos for as long as I can remember. I always got to listen to all his new stories.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Every night, Dad would give me a Zaytun Peach for dinner, and I'd eat it while he told his stories.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: The Zaytun Peaches were delicious, but Dad's stories were really bad. He always uses sentences that are really hard to understand, and... strange uh, metaphors I think they're called?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: But Dad kept on going, telling his stories again and again. One time, he even borrowed a Kamera from Lord Sangemah Bay's shop and got me to take pictures of him in action.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Dad showed me the picture and said that it shall become the precious record of Sumeru's best storyteller early in his career.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Even though I only had Zaytun Peaches to eat and not-so-great stories to listen to, I was happy.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Then, one day, I tried telling Dad a story I came up with.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Dad seemed really excited from the very beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: He looked really happy. He lifted me up high into the air and told me to continue.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: He lifted me up so high that I was looking down at him. As I continued with my story, I saw his expression gradually change.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: And when I got to my favorite part, Dad started crying. I guess he must've been moved by my story.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: When Dad put me back down, I looked up at him again, but now he had a scary look in his eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You remember it so vividly...

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: It's not only Razi. I, too, remember every detail of what happened that day.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: After that, I gradually grew in fame and started making money. I became Sumeru's best storyteller, just as I always dreamed.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Finally, we could afford more than just Zaytun Peaches for dinner...

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: I thought it would make Razi happy.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I was really happy at first... but then everyone started calling me "Tanger's son" instead of "Razi."

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I kinda guessed why, but I also didn't wanna believe it.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Dad got busier with things that had nothing to do with storytelling... Like that request from Acara Crafts.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: So I made up my mind that this time, I just wanna be good old Razi so that Dad will become good old Dad again...

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Instead of Dad the way he is now, starting every story with "Dedicated to my dearest Razi"...

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I prefer my Dad how he used to be, stumbling over words and not knowing how to end the story.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: That's why I decided to keep how I imagined Aranara to look like, a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Paimon gets it now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To sum up, all of Uncle Tanger's fairytales were actually stories written by Razi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And because Razi didn't want Tanger to keep living a lie, he refused to help him with Acara Crafts' commission.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: ...Yes. That's why I tried looking for possible evidence of Aranara. But it turned out that I was just being a clown, as always, and not even a funny one.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: I'm a terrible father.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Razi... I'm so sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: And I owe you all an apology, too, for wasting your time.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Razi's the only one who can help Acara Crafts. If you can manage to persuade him, that is. Right now, I think I just want to find a tree hollow and be quiet for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... are we gonna let this happen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's up to Razi.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: You want me to help Acara Crafts with their carving?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I did mention what the Aranara look like in my stories, but to make a carving, we might need more details...

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: #Collei, {NICKNAME}, and Paimon, I might need your help on this one.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I've never really left Port Ormos before. This is my first time in Gandharva Ville... well, it's my first time being so far from home.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Sumeru is so much bigger than I thought. Seeing new places has given me loads of new ideas for my Aranara stories.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: So I wanna visit more places in Sumeru. That way, I can help Acara Crafts create an Aranara carving that everyone will love.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: And I also wanna take pictures of Dad everywhere that we travel to.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: You... you still want me to come with you? Even after all I've done?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Yeah, of course! C'mon, you're the best Dad ever.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: This is the happiest Razi has sounded since we met him.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: I wanna thank you, Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh? Me? I... I didn't do anything to help.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: You told me about telling my secrets to a tree hollow.

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Even though I didn't have the time to find a tree hollow, telling everyone my secret made me feel so much better.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah... It's hard to keep too many secrets, and there's no need to hide our mistakes from others all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I made a lot of mistakes back in Mondstadt. But when I look back on them, it all feels more like a new beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm sure this experience will be the same for Tanger.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Yes. I'll do my best to become a good father again.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Wait... did you just say you've been to Mondstadt...?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah! Um, I just, uh... just passed by once! Never mind that — come on now, Acara Crafts is waiting for us!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Let's go, Razi! Grab that Kamera and see what hidden inspiration you can discover along the way!

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Okay, let's go! C'mon, Dad!

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: Razi, slow down and watch your step.

choices.text: Looks like everyone's in good spirits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah!

choices.text: Let's catch up with them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Tanger's supposed to be here in Gandharva Ville looking for inspiration, but how do we find him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we... yell his name at the top of our lungs?

choices.text: That sounds like a bad idea.

response.text: Hey buddy, what's your name? What are you doing here all alone? Do you live in Gandharva Ville?
Regardless, don't worry. As a Trainee Forest Ranger, I'll do everything I can to help you.

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: Hi, Miss Forest Ranger! I'm Razi. Don't mind me, I know the way back to Gandharva Ville.
When people say "Don't mind me," what they really mean is "Don't worry about me." That's all the more reason not to leave you alone.
Hey, don't cry... What's wrong? Take your time, you can tell me all about it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That voice sounds familiar... Paimon's heard it somewhere before.

choices.text: We heard it right here in Gandharva Ville.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, it's Collei! And a child who seems to be upset. Let's go say hi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hi, Collei! How have you been?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: #Ah, Paimon and {NICKNAME}! I've been doing pretty well, thanks for asking. I'm helping Master Tighnari patrol the forest. What brings you here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're here on an errand. We heard your voice, so we thought we'd come ask you for help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You seem kinda busy though...

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: Um... I'll be fine. You go help them first, Miss Forest Ranger. I'm okay, really! The sand got into my eyes, that's all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (What a well-mannered child.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We can't just leave him here.)

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Sand? There's not a lot of sand in a forest. You keep saying you're okay because you don't want us to know what you're upset about, right?

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: Maybe...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: That's exactly why you have to get it off your chest.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Here's a trick. If you're keeping a secret that bothers you, you can try telling it all to a tree hollow.

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: A tree hollow?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Yeah, a tree hollow! Do you know Tanger's stories? The Aranara living in the forest will patiently listen to every word children say.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Maybe there really are Aranara living in the tree hollows that will listen to you.

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: You like the Aranara stories, too!?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Of course, I love them!

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: People who like Aranara are the best! Okay... I'll try telling my secrets to a tree hollow. Thanks, Miss Forest Ranger, you know everything!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Hehe... You're just exaggerating. Anyway, I'm trying to be like my friend, who always does her best to cheer people up when they seem sad.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: So, how're you doing? Feeling any better now? The forest is very dangerous, so how about we stick together?

response.speaker: Razi
response.text: Sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Collei's so good with kids.

choices.text: A Forest Ranger you can trust.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Well, helping children who are lost in the rainforest is all part of a Forest Ranger's duty.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: So, what was it you wanted help with? You're not lost too, are you?

choices.text: No, no.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Collei about the situation at Acara Crafts.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Okay, so you're looking for a children's author from Port Ormos called Tanger... and he's here in Gandharva Ville looking for inspiration...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Wait. When you say Tanger... Do you mean "the" Tanger?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, Uncle Tanger!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: So he's in the area? Looking for inspiration for a new story as we speak?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: This is amazing, could you wait for me for a second? I'll run Razi back to Gandharva Ville and then I'll be right back!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I've always been curious what the man behind those incredible stories is like in person.

choices.text: We actually wanna go deeper into the forest.
You handled that expertly.
It's Collei.
We might alert the Forest Rangers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe he's from a wealthy family.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe he's one of Lesser Lord Kusanali's familiars.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: "You can deceive the eyes, but you can't deceive the heart." This line is at the beginning and also the end of "Aranara's Vow."

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: I'm certain that in a hundred years' time, this line will become a famous proverb in Sumeru... don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: Dad never used to be like this... It's all my fault...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm okay, you guys go ahead. I'm just a little tired.

dialogues.speaker: Tanger
dialogues.text: *snore*... *snore*...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We probably shouldn't wake him up.)

dialogues.speaker: Razi
dialogues.text: (Razi's sleeping peacefully.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We probably shouldn't wake him up.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So Tanger headed this way? I know this place pretty well. Follow me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey look, aren't these Collei's footprints? But... why are they headed towards the tree hollow?
